grading_method.policy: grading-policy.md, applied to each current same-local answer/evidence object independently against its literal question, frozen summary, fixed key and supplied primary rulebook; no cross-answer borrowing, no label/keyword scoring, no repairs.
grading_method.scope: Complete material requested parts; natural entailment and unambiguous defined-operation shorthand accepted; unasked key context and exception inventories not required. Missing material parts => partial; material contradictions => incorrect; all requested parts resolved without material contradiction/unsupported guess => correct.
grading_method.unsupported_guesses: Independently assessed against summary; none found. No support label was used as a grade.
grading_method.source_review: Read extracted primary text and selected corresponding supplied PDF pages using pypdf, including setup, structure bonuses, combat, encounters and scoring. No external game evidence used.
grading_method.borderline_notes: Factory setup randomization must be resolved rather than inferred from face-down. Zero-feature payout is a requested schedule amount on Q40/Q41, whereas unasked faction exception inventories and key extras are excluded. See per-part reasoning for accepted scope/equivalence decisions.

grades.question: After you achieve a star goal, may you decline or delay placing that star to avoid ending the game? How does this differ from holding a completed objective card unrevealed?
grades.expected_answer: An earned star must be placed on the appropriate achievement immediately; it cannot be declined or delayed to avoid ending the game. You may instead wait to reveal a completed objective, provided you still satisfy it when you reveal it; when you reveal it, place the star.

grades.observed_answer: No. Place a star as soon as you achieve a star goal; stars are permanent and the sixth immediately ends the game. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but must meet all requirements at the moment you reveal it on your own turn.
